questions.prompt: Alas, the bravest soldiers fell, but their glory remains forever.
questions.answer: Ēheu, fortissimī mīlitēs cecidērunt, sed glōria eōrum in aeternum manet.

questions.prompt: Behold, the messenger arrives, and the whole city rejoices!
questions.answer: Ecce, nūntius advenit, atque tōta urbs gaudet.

questions.prompt: O citizens, defend the fatherland, for the enemy is at the gates!
questions.answer: Ō cīvēs, patriam dēfendite, nam hostis ad portās est.

questions.prompt: See, the swift horseman flies across the plain, and dust rises.
questions.answer: Ēn, vēlōx eques per campum volat, atque pulvis surgit.

questions.prompt: O gods, either grant us victory or let us die bravely!
questions.answer: Ō dī, aut nōbīs victōriam date aut fortiter moriāmur!

questions.prompt: Evoe, the maidens dance for Bacchus, while the wine flows abundantly.
questions.answer: Euoe, virginēs Bacchō saltant, dum vīnum largē fluit.

questions.prompt: Hey you, why do you flee, since the danger has already passed?
questions.answer: Eho, cūr fugis, cum perīculum iam praeterierit?

questions.prompt: Look, a huge serpent glides through the grass, and the shepherds flee.
questions.answer: Ēn, ingēns serpēns per herbam lābitur, et pāstōrēs fugiunt.

questions.prompt: O beautiful goddess, protect the fishermen, for the sea rages fiercely.
questions.answer: Ō pulchra dea, piscātōrēs servā, nam mare ferōciter saevit.

questions.prompt: Ah me, the winter is harsh, yet spring will return with flowers.
questions.answer: Ēheu, hiems trux est, sed vēr cum flōribus redībit.

questions.prompt: Behold, the victor returns crowned, and the crowd shouts loudly.
questions.answer: Ecce, victor corōnātus revertitur, atque turba magnā vōce clāmat.

questions.prompt: Alas, the poet is silent, for the Muse has abandoned him.
questions.answer: Heu, poēta tacet, nam Mūsa eum dēseruit.

questions.prompt: O young men, seize glory, since fortune favors the bold!
questions.answer: Ō iuvenēs, glōriam corripite, quia fortūna audācēs iuvat.

questions.prompt: Hurrah, peace has been made, and the weary soldiers return home.
questions.answer: Iō, pāx facta est, et fessī mīlitēs domum redeunt.

questions.prompt: Look, the fields, surrounded by a river, are green with new leaves.
questions.answer: Ēn, agrī, flūmine circumdatī, novīs foliīs virent.

questions.prompt: Hurrah, we have conquered, and the citizens rejoice throughout the whole city!
questions.answer: Iō, vīcimus, et cīvēs per tōtam urbem gaudent!

questions.prompt: Ah me, the ship, tossed by the waves, was lost with all its sailors.
questions.answer: Ēheu, nāvis, flūctibus iactāta, cum omnibus nautīs āmissa est.

questions.prompt: Alas, the queen weeps, for her son has perished in war.
questions.answer: Ēheu, rēgīna flet, nam fīlius eius bellō periit.

questions.prompt: Behold, the poet sings, and the whole crowd listens in silence.
questions.answer: Ecce, poēta canit, et tōta turba silentiō audit.

questions.prompt: Hey there, friend, why do you flee, since the danger has already departed?
questions.answer: Heus, amīce, cūr fugis, cum perīculum iam abierit?

questions.prompt: Hurrah, the citizens shout, for the tyrant has been driven from the city.
questions.answer: Iō, cīvēs clāmant, nam tyrannus ex urbe pulsus est.

questions.prompt: Oh, how great is the wisdom of the old man whom all revere!
questions.answer: Ō, quanta est sapientia senis quem omnēs venerantur!

questions.prompt: Woe, the fields lie waste, and the weary farmer groans.
questions.answer: Vae, agrī vāstī iacent, et agricola fessus gemit.

questions.prompt: Look, a messenger approaches, bearing letters sealed with wax.
questions.answer: Ēn, nūntius appropinquat, litterās cērā signātās ferēns.
